demo.title: Rendered by the real execution engine
demo.subtitle: This is a recorded simulator run, replayed step by step
python_steps: A list object [1, 2] is created and a points to it.
b = a is not a copy. b points to the same list.
Appending through b changes a too. They are the same object.
a[:] creates a new list. c points to a separate object.
Appending to c leaves a and b untouched.
Output: a and b are equal, only c differs.
javascript_steps: The setTimeout callback goes to the Task Queue and waits.
The .then callback goes to the Microtask Queue.
The remaining synchronous console.log('5') runs first.
Once the call stack is empty, microtasks run first. → '3'
The chained .then is also a microtask. → '4'
Only after all microtasks finish does the task run. → '2'
